title: IFCASL Corpus of French and German Non-native and Native Read Speech
why_promising: Primary French-German bilingual learner/native read-speech corpus of about 100 speakers. The publication reports word- and phone-level segmentation and annotation, with more than 50% of data manually corrected; project reports state that automatic speech-text alignment was followed by manual checking and annotation in both France and Germany. This is directly eligible in principle if the manually checked layers can be isolated from untouched forced-aligned material.
open_question: Locate the public corpus deposit or current access endpoint; enumerate audio/annotation files; isolate manually corrected word/phone tiers from unverified automatic alignments; record speaker/task metadata, correction coverage, licenses, and exact annotation provenance before core promotion.

title: Berlin Dialogue Corpus (BeDiaCo) Version 2
why_promising: Primary German production corpus with 36 participants, topic-led and task-led spontaneous dialogues plus read word lists. Documentation explicitly describes audio plus Praat TextGrid files and a multi-layer annotation architecture including phonetic segmentation, diplomatic transliteration, filler particles, intonation phrases, dialogue structure, word types, and inflectional realization.
open_question: Enumerate the current HU media-repository corpus files and annotation tiers; verify which phonetic boundaries/labels were manually produced or corrected versus automatically generated; preserve v2 lineage and licensing; ingest TextGrid tiers and participant/task metadata only after tier-level provenance is confirmed.
